main_text.p: 2. Is motus potest esse continuus, qui & perfectus est, & in quo nulla occurrit oppositio, nulla intercedit quies media. Huiusmodi autem motus est circularis, atq; is solus. Igitur solus motus circularis potest esse continuus.
main_text.head: Vtrum idem motus circularis & continuus sit primus?
main_text.p: 1. Omnis motus localis aut est circularis, aut rectus, aut reflexus, aut mixtus. Atqui ex his circularis & rectus priores sunt reflexo itèq; mixto, praeterea ex illis duobus circularis prior est recto. Igitur motus circularis erit motus primus. Minoris posterius membrum, uidelicet quòd circularis motus sit prior recto, ita probatur: Motus rectus est imperfectus & corruptus. Talis autem non est motus circularis. Igitur motus circularis praestat recto. Maior probatur: Imperfectus est motus rectus: quia cum non possit dari motus rectus infinitus (propterea quòd neq; linea infinita esse potest, per quam talis motus diduceretur,) semper potest illi aliqua accedere additio. Corruptus autem est motus rectus: quia ad terminum magnitudinis cum perucnerit, ibi c ssat. In motum autem circularem nihil horum competere, per se manifestum est.
2. Motus qui potest esse perpetuus, prior est eo qui non potest esse perpetuus. Motus autem circularis

page.notes: Printed header reads "164" at left and "AND. HYPERII" at head. Page number 164 is at the top left. A small mark "ssat" near the middle of paragraph 1 is a fragment of a word ("ibi c ssat"), rendered as printed; the reading "ibi cessat" is likely but I did not read it clearly, so the text is left as the scan shows. The last line "laris" at the right of the foot is the start of a word broken at the page end ("circu-laris") and continues on the next page, so it is copied as a fragment. The word "perucnerit" is as printed. The small mark at the bottom centre is an ornament, not text. Words in paragraph 2 near the page edge are partly faint; the transcription follows the most legible reading. Heading "Vtrum idem motus circularis & continuus sit primus?" is set centred in larger type. The page has a typographic ornament with no text, and the lowercase line "Imo,idq;" is printed with an italic ligature. Reading of "ibi c ssat" is uncertain and marked here rather than in the text.
